AttributeField.description:
An attribute of each pair's observed series, to group or filter by (e.g. a state).

``of: series`` (default) reads it from the observed dataset's series table; ``of:
location`` from the series' location in the dataset's locations layer. Constant per
series; null where the series or location has none.

attribute.description: The column in the series table or layer.
attribute.title: Attribute

AttributeField.title: AttributeField

Bootstrap.description:
Bootstrap confidence intervals for a stage's metrics (shared resamples).

Every group is resampled ``reps`` times, the same way for every metric in the
stage. Results depend only on ``seed`` and the group's key, never on how the work
was split up.

block.description: Block length for block methods. Whole days (e.g. P7D) or calendar months (e.g. P1M, P3M) resample those periods of value_time, empty ones included, and can come from stored state; another duration (e.g. PT12H) is converted to rows from each group's time span; a number is rows.
block.title: Block

method.description: iid resamples pairs; circular_block resamples fixed-length blocks (wrapping around); stationary uses random block lengths with mean `block`; year_block (alias gumboot) resamples whole (water) years, keeping each year's seasonality.
method.title: Method

min_count.description: Groups with fewer forecast cases (pairs, for deterministic forecasts) get null intervals.
min_count.title: Min Count

min_years.description: year_block: groups spanning fewer years get null intervals.
min_years.title: Min Years

sort_by.description: Pair columns that order each group before resampling blocks.
sort_by.title: Sort By

year_start_month.description: year_block: the month years start in (10 = US water year; 1 = calendar).
year_start_month.title: Year Start Month

Bootstrap.title: Bootstrap

year_start_month.description: The month a year starts: water_year default 10, quarter default 1.
year_start_month.title: Year Start Month

CalendarField.title: CalendarField

ChangeField.description:
Each value's change over a window within its series: ``value(t) - value(t - window)``.

``side: primary`` uses each primary series; ``side: secondary`` each forecast trajectory
(dataset, series, reference time and member or quantile). Null when the series has no
value exactly ``window`` earlier. With the metrics' ``values`` option, contingency
metrics then score ramps: a change of at least the threshold.
ChangeField.title: ChangeField

ColumnRef.description: A pair column holding a per-pair value (e.g. a flood threshold or a capacity).
ColumnRef.title: ColumnRef

ConditionsField.description:
Overlapping subsets: each pair is copied into every level whose condition it meets.

``levels`` maps a label to a SQL condition (checked like ``filter``), e.g.
``above_q95: "primary_value > q95"``; with ``all`` (default true) every pair also counts
in a level labelled ``all``. Unlike other fields a pair can be in several levels, so
grouping by the field scores each level over its own pairs (a pair above q95 counts
in ``above_q85`` too). Conditions may use any other field: the copies are made after
every other field and before ``filter``, which can keep a level (``flow =
'above_q95'``). Several conditions fields multiply (each pair in every combination).
ConditionsField.title: ConditionsField

EventsField.description:
Events: runs of values at or above a threshold, labelled per series.

Each pair inside an event gets the event's id (``<series>@<start>``); others get
null, so ``group_by`` the field scores each event and ``filter`` keeps event pairs.
``threshold`` is a value with its unit (``{value: v, unit: u}``), ``{quantile: q}`` of
each series' own values (in the evaluated window), or ``{column: c}``: a pair column
such as a ``percentile`` field, for a threshold from the series' whole record. Runs
separated by less than ``merge_gap`` join into one event (the gap included); events
shorter than ``min_duration`` are dropped.
EventsField.title: EventsField

ExceedanceField.description:
Each value's exceedance probability within its series.

Weibull plotting position: rank (largest first, ties share the lower rank) / (n + 1)
over the series' distinct times. ``side: primary`` ranks each primary series;
``side: secondary`` ranks each forecast trajectory (dataset, series, reference time and
member or quantile). Computed over the pairs being evaluated (the evaluated window).
ExceedanceField.title: ExceedanceField

ExprField.description: A row-level field computed from a SQL expression.
ExprField.title: ExprField

GeneratedInput.description:
A secondary dataset generated from the observations: a reference for skill scores.

- ``persistence`` (``like``): for every forecast in ``like`` (series, reference time,
  value time), the last observation at or before the reference time, for the
  observed series linked to that forecast series. Computed within the run from the
  observations it reads.
- ``climatology`` (``from``): a stored climatology dataset (one value per series, day
  of year and hour, built over the period of record) looked up at each observation's
  day of year and hour. No reference times, so it can't be grouped by lead time.
- ``blend`` (``like`` and ``from``): the optimal combination of persistence and
  climatology (Yang et al. 2020), on the grid of ``like``: climatology at the value
  time plus the persistence anomaly (observation minus climatology at the reference
  time) damped by the anomalies' autocorrelation at that lead, fitted per observed
  series and whole-hour lead from the observations the run reads.

Persistence (and so the blend) uses observations complete by the reference time: an
instantaneous value at or before it, or a value over a period whose window has ended.
Pairs of generated inputs are keyed by the observed series.

filter.description: Expression applied before pairing; numbers compared with value are in the variable's canonical unit.
filter.title: Filter

like.description: persistence: a forecast dataset whose grid (series, reference times, value times) the persistence forecast copies.
like.title: Like

max_age.description: persistence (and blend): use only an observation at most this old at the reference time, e.g. PT2H for hourly forecasts. Set it: without it a run can't limit the observations it reads to the forecasts' span (an observation from any time before may be used), so it reads every series' whole record, which can be many times the data and memory the evaluation needs.
max_age.title: Max Age

GeneratedInput.title: GeneratedInput

Guard.description:
Null metrics where a group's data is too thin to trust them, and say why.

Conditions apply to each group's observations; ``metrics`` (output names) limits
which metrics a guard nulls (default: all of the stage's). A tripped guard nulls the
metrics and their bootstrap intervals, and the stage's ``null_reason`` column says
why, e.g. ``nse, kge: obs std 0.004 < 0.01``.

min_obs_mean.description: Observed mean at least this (e.g. for relative metrics).
min_obs_mean.title: Min Obs Mean

min_obs_std.description: Observed standard deviation at least this (e.g. for NSE, KGE, correlation, which divide by the observations' variability).
min_obs_std.title: Min Obs Std

Guard.title: Guard

InputRef.description: A dataset used as input, optionally filtered.

filter.description: Expression applied before pairing; numbers compared with value are in the variable's canonical unit.
filter.title: Filter

InputRef.title: InputRef

Inputs.description:
The primary dataset (usually observations) and one or more secondary datasets.

Pairing sides are named ``primary`` and ``secondary`` (paired columns ``primary_*`` and
``secondary_*``), shared with the TEEHR team. A dataset's role (observed, simulated,
forecast) still says what its data is.

primary.description: The dataset scored against: usually observations.

secondary.description: Datasets scored against the primary one (simulations or forecasts). Each becomes a value of the 'secondary_dataset' column in pairs.
secondary.title: Secondary

Inputs.title: Inputs

LeadTimeBinsField.title: LeadTimeBinsField

MetricSpec.description: A metric (first stage) or summary (later stages) with options.

estimator.description: crps: standard (default) or fair (unbiased for the ensemble size).
estimator.title: Estimator

exceedance.description: fdc_slope: exceedance probabilities [e1, e2], 0 < e1 < e2 < 1.
exceedance.title: Exceedance

interval.description: Interval metrics: the central interval's quantile levels, default [0.05, 0.95].
interval.title: Interval

log.description: fdc_slope: the log form (default true) or the linear slope (false).
log.title: Log

missing_day_threshold.description: Timing metrics: the fraction of a year's days that may be missing before the year is left out (default 0.1).
missing_day_threshold.title: Missing Day Threshold

name.description: A metric's canonical name or one of its aliases (e.g. rmse for root_mean_square_error); results carry the canonical name. Later stages: a summary.
name.title: Name

normalize_by.description: nmae/nrmse: mean_primary (default), range_primary, a value with its unit (e.g. installed capacity, {value: 500, unit: "MW"}) or {column: <pair column>} (its group mean).
normalize_by.title: Normalize By

of.description: Later stages only: column to summarize.
of.title: Of

rank.description: rank_frequency: the observation's rank among ensemble members (0 = below all members).
rank.title: Rank

sa.description: KGE family: weight on the variability term (default 1).
sa.title: Sa

sb.description: KGE family: weight on the bias term (default 1).
sb.title: Sb

scale.description: mase: the column holding each pair's naive scale (a naive_scale field).

sr.description: KGE family: weight on the correlation term (default 1).
sr.title: Sr

threshold.description: Contingency metrics: event threshold (value >= threshold): a value with its unit ({value: 1000, unit: "[cft_i]/s"}), {column: <pair column>} or {primary_quantile: 0.9} (per group).
threshold.title: Threshold

transform.description: First stage only: transform primary and secondary values before the metric (log is natural; inv is reciprocal).

values.description: First stage only: compute the metric on these pair columns instead of primary_value and secondary_value, e.g. change fields for ramps.

year_start_month.description: Annual metrics: first month of the year (1 = calendar, 10 = water year).
year_start_month.title: Year Start Month

MetricSpec.title: MetricSpec

NaiveScaleField.description:
Each pair's in-sample naive scale, for MASE.

The observed series' stored mean ``|y(t) - y(t - lag)|`` over a training period, from
a ``naive_scale`` dataset, converted to the observed unit.

lag.description: The naive forecast's lag, as built (e.g. PT1H, P1D).
lag.title: Lag

NaiveScaleField.title: NaiveScaleField

ObsQuantile.description: A quantile of each group's observations.
ObsQuantile.title: ObsQuantile

attributes.description: With geometry: attributes of the same place to add as result columns, e.g. a basin's name, from the layer the geometry comes from.
attributes.title: Attributes

geometry.description: Give each result row a geometry, by a column of the final stage's group_by: a within field (its polygon) or primary_series_key (the observed series' location). Looked up once per result row; results then come as GeoJSON on request.
geometry.title: Geometry

pairs.description: Whether a saved evaluation's runs keep their pairs in the project lake: 'all' or 'none'. Unset uses the platform default. First-stage rows and results are always kept; without pairs, drill-down re-pairs on request.
pairs.title: Pairs

unit.description: Unit to evaluate in (e.g. 'm3/s'): primary and secondary values are converted to it before fields and metrics, and thresholds and normalizers (which carry their own unit) are converted to it too. Default: the observed dataset's unit. An input filter's numbers are in its variable's canonical unit.
unit.title: Unit

Pairing.description: How predicted series are matched to observed series.

common_sample.description: Score every secondary input on the same sample: keep only observations (primary series and value time) that every secondary input paired with, after filters. A forecast missing on hard days then can't look better for it.
common_sample.title: Common Sample

on_attribute.description: Series catalog attribute shared by primary and secondary series.
on_attribute.title: On Attribute

relation.description: Crosswalk dataset mapping primary (left) to secondary (right) keys.
relation.title: Relation

Pairing.title: Pairing

PercentileField.description:
Each pair's stored percentile of its observed series, over its period of record.

From a ``percentiles`` dataset (built over the whole record, so not limited to the
evaluated window), converted to the observed unit; null for series without one (too
short a record). Non-exceedance: the 90th is the value not exceeded 90% of the time.
Use it as a threshold: ``{column: <name>}``.
PercentileField.title: PercentileField

Quantity.description:
A value with its unit (a UCUM symbol), e.g. ``{value: 1000, unit: "[cft_i]/s"}``.

Building the plan converts it to the evaluation unit (``output.unit``, else the
primary dataset's), so a spec means the same thing whatever unit its data are in.
Quantity.title: Quantity

Reduce.description:
Reduce each window of pairs to a statistic before the metrics (e.g. its peak).

The pairs are grouped by ``by`` (a forecast window: series, reference time, lead-time
bin...), and each window becomes one pair per statistic in ``stats``: its mean, min,
max or sum of observed and of predicted values, labelled in a ``stat`` column. Metrics
then score those reduced pairs. Applied after ``filter`` and conditions, before a
rollup's copies.

by.description: Columns that make a window; must include primary_series_key. The predicted dataset and series, members, quantiles and conditions fields are added.
by.title: By

Reduce.title: Reduce

SeriesQuantile.description: A quantile of each series' own values (in the evaluated window).
SeriesQuantile.title: SeriesQuantile

Skill.description:
Skill scores of each secondary dataset against a reference dataset.

For each listed metric, ``<metric>_skill = 1 - score / score_of_reference`` (or
``<metric>_ratio = score / score_of_reference`` with ``form: ratio``), comparing rows
that match on every group_by column except ``secondary_dataset``.

lag.description: Autocovariance lags in the test's (Newey-West) variance, in time steps; default floor(4 (n / 100)^(2/9)).
lag.title: Lag

loss.description: The test's loss: squared or absolute error.
loss.title: Loss

matched.description: Compare each dataset with the reference only on observations both forecast (same observed series and value_time within a group), recomputing both scores on those; the metric columns themselves stay unmatched.
matched.title: Matched

metrics.description: Output columns of error metrics in this stage (a metric's alias names its canonical column).
metrics.title: Metrics

reference.description: A secondary input dataset, e.g. a persistence forecast.
reference.title: Reference

test.description: dm: Diebold-Mariano test of each dataset's loss against the reference's on the observations both forecast; adds dm_statistic (negative: the dataset's errors are smaller) and dm_p_value (two-sided).
test.title: Test

Skill.title: Skill

bootstrap.description: First stage only: bootstrap intervals for its metrics.

grouping_sets.description: First stage only: the general form of rollup, each set the columns a row is grouped by (besides group_by); [] aggregates across all of them.
grouping_sets.title: Grouping Sets

guards.description: First stage only: null metrics on too little or too flat data, with a null_reason column.
guards.title: Guards

rollup.description: First stage only: also aggregate across these columns, coarsest first, as SQL ROLLUP: rollup [water_year, quarter] gives rows by quarter, by water year and for all. Each row's set is named in a 'grouping' column, and a column it's aggregated across reads '(all)'. Folded into grouping_sets and group_by.
rollup.title: Rollup

skill.description: First stage only: skill scores against a reference dataset.

TimeMatch.description: How predicted values are aligned with observed values in time.
TimeMatch.title: TimeMatch

Transform.description:
Transform applied to obs and pred before a metric is computed (the shared list).

Pairs where the transform is undefined or not finite (``log`` of a non-positive
value, ``exp`` overflowing) are excluded from that metric only.
Transform.title: Transform

ValuesRef.description: Pair columns a metric reads instead of ``primary_value`` and ``secondary_value``.
ValuesRef.title: ValuesRef

WithinField.description:
The polygon of a layer each pair's observed series is in, to group by (e.g. a basin).

Each series' location (the observed dataset's locations layer; a line or polygon by
its centroid) is matched to the polygons of ``layer`` that contain it, boundaries
included. The value is that polygon's ``attribute`` (default its key); where polygons
overlap, the one with the smallest key; null when no polygon contains the location.

attribute.description: The polygon attribute to label with (its key).
attribute.title: Attribute

layer.description: A polygon layer: name, or public.<name>.
layer.title: Layer

WithinField.title: WithinField

reduce.description: Reduce each window of pairs to statistics before metrics.
